title: Explicit Physical Knowledge in Machine Learning for Ocean Carbon Flux Reconstruction: The pCO2-Residual Method
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
processes: temperature-dependent solubility and carbonate chemical equilibrium
testbed_rationale: The study produces an observation-based spatial reconstruction and gap-filling product of surface ocean pCO2 and CO2 fluxes rather than high-resolution simulation data for subgrid parameterization or dynamic model emulation.
pain_points: Severe spatial and temporal sparsity of in situ pCO2 observations, particularly in the Southern Hemisphere during winter
Missing satellite chlorophyll observations prior to 1998 and polar winter darkness gaps, requiring climatology and interpolation that introduce uncertainty (~0.1 PgC/yr)
Competing physical effects where SST has both direct thermodynamic impacts on pCO2 and indirect correlation through stratification and mixing
Piston velocity and wind product uncertainty driving substantial regional uncertainty in air-sea CO2 flux calculations
Uncertainty in riverine outgassing correction (0.49 ± 0.26 PgC/yr) when estimating anthropogenic fluxes from net flux products
extraction_notes: The study develops a physics-informed residual learning scheme: it calculates the direct temperature effect (pCO2-T) analytically via the Takahashi formulation, uses XGBoost to learn the remaining biogeochemical/physical residual (pCO2-Residual), and adds them back together.
